tasks.task: I need to quickly validate a simple customer-support SLA rule set before a 30-minute ops review. Use the active engine “swipl-local” (id pleng_01J3G2Q4YH3E7R6H9K8P1S2T3V), create a fresh session with a 1800-second TTL, load a program where vip_customer/1 marks alice as VIP and uses the existing priority/2 + sla_minutes/2 logic (60 minutes for VIP/high, 240 otherwise), then query the SLA for ticket(alice) and ticket(bob). Finally, confirm the session is still ready and has the loaded program.

success_criteria: Step 1 returns engine.id = pleng_01J3G2Q4YH3E7R6H9K8P1S2T3V and engine.status = "active".
Step 2 returns a session with expires_at reflecting ~1800 seconds TTL (or capped per policy) and session.status = "ready".
Step 3 returns program.compile_status = "loaded" and session.loaded_program_id equals the returned program.id.
Step 4 query succeeds and returns a binding where M = 60 for ticket(alice).
Step 5 query succeeds and returns a binding where M = 240 for ticket(bob).
Step 6 returns session.status = "ready" and session.loaded_program_id equals $2.program.id.

args.program:
% customer support triage + SLA validation
vip_customer(alice).

priority(ticket(Id),high) :- vip_customer(Id), !.
priority(ticket(_),normal).

sla_minutes(ticket(Id),60) :- priority(ticket(Id),high), !.
sla_minutes(ticket(_),240).

tasks.task: I need to run a quick genealogy check before my report goes out in 15 minutes: on the active engine “swipl-local” please create a new 1-hour session, load a small family tree (ada→bea→cai), and confirm via queries that ada is an ancestor of cai and that there are no siblings for bea. After loading, also list the user predicates that were made available.

success_criteria: A new session is created on engine pleng_01J3G2Q4YH3E7R6H9K8P1S2T3V (“swipl-local”) with ~3600s TTL.
The program load succeeds (compile_status='loaded') in the created session.
discover(session_id=<created>, origin='user_program') returns predicate entries including ancestor/2 and parent/2 (and sibling/2 if cached).
Query 'ancestor(ada,cai).' returns status='succeeded' (at least one solution / true).
Query 'sibling(bea,_).' returns status indicating no solutions (failed / empty bindings), demonstrating bea has no siblings under the loaded facts.

args.program:
parent(ada,bea).
parent(bea,cai).
ancestor(X,Y) :- parent(X,Y).
ancestor(X,Y) :- parent(X,Z), ancestor(Z,Y).
% sibling rule included to test 'no siblings for bea'
sibling(X,Y) :- parent(P,X), parent(P,Y), X \= Y.
